correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the proof. The determinant factorization makes the estimator conditionally unbiased and the Gaussian quadratic-form variance is twice the squared Frobenius norm of log M. Almost surely ker(U^T) in the spike block has dimension (r-ell)_+ and gives exactly that many forced eigenvalues 1+t in a reducing subspace. In its orthogonal complement substituting c=U^+a into the Nyström residual variational formula bounds the residual by (1+||VU^+||^2)I; the inverse congruence is contractive since P>=I and preserves the complement. The remaining eigenvalues lie in [1,2+||VU^+||^2]. The least positive singular value of U dominates that of a square Gaussian subblock by Gram matrix monotonicity. Its inverse norm has a half moment by the adjugate bound, Hölder exponents 3 and 3/2 and the QR chi-product negative determinant moment of order 3/4, including a final chi with one degree of freedom. Independence of U and V and log^2(2+z^2)=O(1+z^(1/2)) give the contrast-uniform expected bound including the square case ell=r. This yields the exact diverging coefficient and both directions of the threshold.
residual_risks: Fixed finite dimensions and exact arithmetic only. The 1,008 seeded checks test finite matrix identities and conditional risk, not probe-frequency statistics or existence of a uniform expected bound. No formal proof certificate is claimed.

value.rationale: The benchmark isolates exactly how many sketch directions are needed to prevent contrast-driven one-probe variance, even when ordinary square Gaussian inverse moments are too strong to use. The logarithmic observable permits a sharp conclusion at the no-excess-sketch boundary, and the exact coefficient distinguishes failure to capture the spike subspace from bounded error on the remainder. This is more than reproducing the dimension-two example or the ideal spectral benchmark.
residual_risks: Does not provide dimension-uniform constants, cost comparisons, or a guarantee with Lanczos truncation or finite precision.
